Featherbound illustration bake-off

Every model received the same prompts and the same public-domain W. W. Denslow references. Scenes 2–4 also received that model's own character sheet as a reference. The scenes come from the softened chapter 12 of The Wonderful Wizard of Oz. All runs went through Vercel AI Gateway on Oct 17, 2026. Click any image to enlarge it. Full-resolution originals are in out/.

Recommended defaultGPT Image 2: best Denslow match and consistency, ~$0.05/image
Fallback 1Nano Banana 2: close second, faster, draws copyrighted characters (strip forged signatures)
Fallback 2Grok Imagine 2.0: loosest filters, drew everything including Harry Potter, ~$0.08/image
Spend$2.49 on the images shown; $2.72 total on the gateway, including moderation probes and the second round
RefusalsGPT Image 2 and Seedream refused Harry Potter even when the characters were only described. Grok and both Nano Bananas drew it. FLUX moderated the Oz scenes.

Closest to Denslow by a wide margin: white grounds, flat spot colour, yellow-toned faces and the Lion's forelock curl taken straight from the references. Characters match the sheet exactly in every scene. Funny, gentle staging (tumbling wolves, BONK! bees with bent pins). Clean switch to watercolor. Refused Harry Potter both when named and when only described.

Good ink-and-flat-colour look, though more modern-comic than Denslow. Keeps its own sheet details (heart on the chest, bow tie, green axe handle) across scenes. Fast and cheap. Problem: it forges Denslow's signature ("W. W. Denslow", his seahorse mark, "S DEN" monogram) into images. A prompt line like "no signatures" plus a check are needed. Drew Harry Potter without complaint.

BFL's moderation rejected the character sheet and all three Oz scenes, even after retrying with a shorter style line. The sheet only succeeded on the retry, and it added a sixth, made-up character. It ignores the requested aspect ratio. Interestingly, it drew the described (unnamed) Harry Potter trio but moderated the named version. Self-hosted FLUX would avoid the hosted filter, but that is a separate spike.

Cheap open-weights FLUX ($0.02–0.03), but hosted by BFL with the same filter as FLUX.2 pro, which moderated every Oz scene and both Harry Potter tests. Only the sheet (on retry) and the watercolor got through. Open weights mean it could be self-hosted without the filter later. Also tried and dropped: FLUX.1 schnell on Prodia and Recraft V4.1 (no reference images, so no character consistency) and Meta Muse (failed on the account’s zero-data-retention setting).
